_serves_note: FOUND BY DOING THIS LIFT, AND IT WAS BROKEN ON EVERY STUDIO. canvas.html fetches /canvas-license.json; this provider answers it (export-server.mjs:664) and deliberately returns {} rather than 404 because the canvas probe's console gate treats a 404 as an error. But NO app ever declared it, and it is not an /api/ path — so studio.mjs:474 finds no `serves` prefix, :475 skips it (the sole-provider fallback covers /api/ ONLY), and :479 hands it to the SDK runtime, which 404s. The provider's own defensive answer was unreachable. WHY IT STAYED INVISIBLE: unkeyed tldraw only unmounts the editor on a PRODUCTION https non-loopback origin, so on 127.0.0.1 dev it looks perfect and on a deployed box CANVAS DIES AFTER 5 SECONDS. Same family as `rig ps` needing -A: a dev machine cannot see it. Declaring the route is half the fix; the box must also carry the canvas-license.json file, which is operator-side and separate.
_verbs_note: THIS LIST IS DELIBERATELY 36 OF THE 43 VERBS THIS FILE ANSWERS, AND THE GAP IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT. Withheld: /api/note, /api/note/done, /api/note/flush, /api/note/reconciled, /api/receivers, /api/reveal-file, /api/shell-mtime. The first four reach `execFile("rig", ["queue","create", ...])` — live at export-server.mjs:459, :497 and :534 — so declaring them lets a Studio surface inject work into the rig's coordination system. /api/reveal-file runs `open -R`, which is macOS Finder and meaningless on the Linux boxes we ship to. THE CHOICE IS BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING, WHICH IS THE POINT: on a multi-provider box (host + video + cutdown, i.e. every deployed studio) these seven ALREADY do not route today, because no app declares them and studio.mjs's sole-provider fallback needs exactly one provider. Declaring them here would ENABLE something currently unreachable — a policy change smuggled inside a format migration. A migration changes where a fact is written, never what the product does. THE SCOPE QUESTION IS GENUINELY OPEN and is NOT settled by this file: OQ-5 excluded the note verbs, but it was ruled under the threat model that Ruling 15 later RETRACTED, and that retraction says rig-injection is a FEATURE on a trusted box. So the exclusion rests on a withdrawn premise and the inclusion has never been ruled on its own merits. Routed rather than decided here.
_seeds_note: sdk-impl moved first-run seeding off a hardcoded path onto a provider declaration (SDK 254c280). Until this file existed the boot tool carried THIS provider's file name, module export and marker as literals, which made first-run seeding a video-studio feature no other kind of studio could use. `marker` is the file whose presence means already-seeded; seeding runs only into an absent or empty directory, so a directory with contents and no marker is somebody's data and the box refuses rather than seeding over it.
_seeds_upstream_defect: 🟢 RESOLVED SAME DAY (sdk-impl 58130c4) — KEPT RATHER THAN DELETED, because the reasoning is why the declaration is shaped this way and a future reader would otherwise re-litigate it. WHAT WAS WRONG: compose-rail.mjs copied only run/serves/verbs off a provider.json, so the top-level `seeds` this contract documents never reached studio.mjs, which read `spec.run?.seeds ?? spec.seeds`. Measured both ways on one boot: top level gave the LEGACY hardcoded-path warning and seeded via fallback; the identical block under `run.seeds` gave 'seeded (declared by …)'. I SHIPPED THE DOCUMENTED SHAPE ANYWAY and did not nest, because nesting works today and ships a second undocumented shape for one fact — the defect this migration removes. THAT CALL IS NOW LOAD-BEARING: sdk-impl's fix makes the reader accept ONLY the documented shape, so `run.seeds` no longer works at all. Nesting would have shipped a manifest that broke on their next commit. RE-MEASURED under 58130c4: 'seeded: <root> (declared by @openrig/studio-video)', no legacy warning, timeline.json created. THE DIAGNOSIS WORTH KEEPING, and it is sdk-impl's: a PERMISSIVE READER HID A BROKEN WRITER. `a ?? b` tolerated two shapes without anyone checking which one the composer could actually produce, so NEITHER branch could fire and the failure waited for a real migration to surface it. A reader that accepted only the documented shape would have failed the first time anyone declared one.
_why_this_file_exists: Three apps — canvas, media-manager and mini-nle — each carried a byte-identical copy of the run spec above, because an app was the only place the format let you write it. Three copies of one fact drift, and the drift is silent: the same shape already cost us live rig state when retiring the AGENTS app deleted the only declaration of {{state}} and Matti's landing page served an invented rig under a green live signal. The provider is authoritative about how to start itself; an app is a client that names it.
